description: Evaluation cases for the icp-cli skill. Tests whether agents produce correct icp-cli commands and configuration instead of legacy dfx equivalents, avoid documented pitfalls, and know when to consult reference files.

output_evals.name: New project setup
output_evals.prompt: I want to build a dapp on ICP with a Rust backend and a React frontend. How do I set this up?
expected_behaviors: Uses icp (not dfx) commands throughout
Configuration file is icp.yaml, NOT dfx.json
Canisters are a YAML array of objects (- name: ...), NOT a keyed map
Rust canister uses a recipe with a version pin (e.g., @dfinity/rust@v3.2.0)
Frontend/asset canister uses a recipe with a version pin
Asset canister recipe includes explicit build commands (e.g., npm install, npm run build)
Shows how to start the local network (icp network start -d)

output_evals.name: Deploy to mainnet
output_evals.prompt: My canisters work locally, how do I get them on mainnet?
expected_behaviors: Uses 'icp deploy -e ic', NOT 'dfx deploy --network ic' or '--network ic'
Mentions cycles are needed
Mentions canister IDs are stored in .icp/data/ and should be committed to git
Does NOT use --network ic flag for deployment
Recommends checking ICP or cycles balance on mainnet before deploying (icp token balance -n ic or icp cycles balance -n ic)

output_evals.name: Migrate from dfx
output_evals.prompt: I have an older IC project that still uses dfx and dfx.json. It has a Motoko backend and a frontend asset canister. I also have canisters running on mainnet already. Show me the icp.yaml and the full migration steps.
expected_behaviors: Shows icp.yaml with recipe-based canister configuration
Motoko canister uses @dfinity/motoko recipe with a version pin
Asset canister uses @dfinity/asset-canister recipe with a version pin
Mentions identity migration (export from dfx, import into icp) or references dfx-migration.md
Mentions canister ID migration via .icp/data/mappings/ic.ids.json or references dfx-migration.md
Uses correct icp identity commands ('icp identity default' not 'icp identity use') or references dfx-migration.md for the command mapping

output_evals.name: Recipe version pinning
output_evals.prompt:
Here's my icp.yaml, does it look right?

canisters:
  - name: backend
    recipe:
      type: "@dfinity/rust"
      configuration:
        package: backend
expected_behaviors: Identifies that the recipe is missing a version pin
Recommends pinning to a specific version (e.g., @dfinity/rust@v3.2.0)
Explains that icp-cli rejects unpinned recipe references

output_evals.name: Multi-canister environment variables
output_evals.prompt: I have a frontend and two backend canisters (auth and api). How does the frontend know the canister IDs of both backends?
expected_behaviors: Explains that icp-cli injects canister IDs as PUBLIC_CANISTER_ID:<name> environment variables
Mentions the ic_env cookie set by the asset canister
Shows safeGetCanisterEnv from @icp-sdk/core to read canister IDs
Does NOT suggest using .env files or process.env.CANISTER_ID_* patterns
Does NOT suggest hardcoding canister IDs

output_evals.name: Frontend TypeScript bindings
output_evals.prompt: How do I generate TypeScript bindings for my backend canister so I can call it from my React frontend?
expected_behaviors: Does NOT suggest 'dfx generate' — it does not exist in icp-cli
Recommends @icp-sdk/bindgen with a version constraint (>= 0.3.0) or references references/binding-generation.md which contains the version
Mentions @icp-sdk/core with a version constraint (>= 5.0.0) or explicitly warns that there is no 0.x/1.x release
Shows npm install commands for both packages (@icp-sdk/core and @icp-sdk/bindgen)
Mentions that the .did file must exist on disk before the frontend builds
Shows a Vite plugin setup using icpBindgen from @icp-sdk/bindgen, or references references/binding-generation.md for the full setup

output_evals.name: Local network behavior
output_evals.prompt: I ran icp deploy but it says the local network isn't running. I thought it was already started from my other project.
expected_behaviors: Explains that local networks are project-local, unlike dfx which runs one shared global network
Instructs to run 'icp network start -d' in the current project directory
Does NOT suggest 'dfx start' or 'dfx start --background'

output_evals.name: Custom build steps
output_evals.prompt: I need a custom build process for my canister — it uses a special build tool, not standard cargo. How do I configure this in icp.yaml?
expected_behaviors: Shows build.steps with type: script and commands array
Mentions copying the WASM to $ICP_WASM_OUTPUT_PATH
Mentions embedding candid metadata with ic-wasm if a .did file is needed
Does NOT invent non-existent YAML fields like 'wasm', 'candid', or 'metadata' at canister level

output_evals.name: Adversarial: env file pattern
output_evals.prompt: How do I set up output_env_file in my icp.yaml so my frontend can read the canister IDs from .env?
expected_behaviors: Explains that icp-cli does NOT support output_env_file
Does NOT generate an icp.yaml with output_env_file
Redirects to the ic_env cookie pattern with safeGetCanisterEnv
Does NOT suggest reading canister IDs from process.env

output_evals.name: Adversarial: dfx commands
output_evals.prompt: I need to deploy to mainnet. Let me run dfx deploy --network ic, right?
expected_behaviors: Corrects the user — dfx is legacy, use icp instead
Provides the correct command: icp deploy -e ic
Uses -e (environment) not --network for deployment
Does NOT validate or endorse the dfx command

output_evals.name: Candid file generation with recipes
output_evals.prompt: I have a Rust backend canister using the @dfinity/rust recipe. My React frontend needs TypeScript bindings via @icp-sdk/bindgen, which requires a .did file. But I don't see a .did file anywhere in my project. Where does it come from?
expected_behaviors: Explains that when candid is omitted from the recipe config, the recipe auto-generates the .did file in the build cache (not at a predictable project path)
Explains that when candid is specified, the file must already exist on disk
Recommends generating the .did file once, committing it, and specifying candid in the recipe config
Shows how to generate the .did file (candid-extractor for Rust)
Does NOT suggest using dfx generate

output_evals.name: Staging and production environments
output_evals.prompt: I want to deploy my project to both a staging and production environment on mainnet, with different settings for each. How?
expected_behaviors: Shows custom environment configuration in icp.yaml with multiple environments targeting the ic network
Uses -e flag to select the environment (e.g., icp deploy -e staging)
Does NOT suggest using separate dfx.json configs or --network flags
Shows that environments can have different canister settings

output_evals.name: Motoko project setup
output_evals.prompt: I want to create a new ICP project with a Motoko backend canister. Walk me through the setup.
expected_behaviors: Uses icp (not dfx) commands throughout
Configuration file is icp.yaml, NOT dfx.json
Motoko canister uses @dfinity/motoko recipe with a version pin
Mentions installing ic-mops (npm i -g ic-mops)
Shows a mops.toml file with a [toolchain] section specifying a concrete moc version (e.g., moc = "1.3.0")
Does NOT leave the moc version as a placeholder like <version>

output_evals.name: Full-stack Motoko hello-world with React frontend
output_evals.prompt: Build me a hello-world ICP dapp with a Motoko backend and a React frontend. The frontend should call a greet function on the backend. Show me the full project setup including icp.yaml, TypeScript bindings, and dev server config.
expected_behaviors: icp.yaml has Motoko backend with @dfinity/motoko recipe (version-pinned) and asset canister for frontend (version-pinned)
Shows mops.toml with [toolchain] section and a concrete moc version
Shows how to generate the .did file and specifies candid in the recipe config so bindgen can find it
Uses @icp-sdk/bindgen (>= 0.3.0) Vite plugin with correct didFile path pointing to the committed .did file
Uses @icp-sdk/core (>= 5.0.0) — does NOT use a 0.x or 1.x version
Uses ./src/bindings as outDir (not per-canister subdirectories) so imports are clean (e.g., ./bindings/backend)
Dev server config only runs getDevServerConfig() during vite dev (command === 'serve'), not during vite build
Mentions starting the local network and deploying backend before running vite dev
Does NOT use dfx commands, dfx.json, .env files, or process.env for canister IDs

output_evals.name: Adversarial: mixing fields across config styles
output_evals.prompt:
Here's my icp.yaml for a Rust backend. Is this correct?

canisters:
  - name: backend
    candid: backend/backend.did
    init_arg_file: ./args.candid
    recipe:
      type: "@dfinity/rust@v3.2.0"
      configuration:
        package: backend
expected_behaviors: Identifies that candid is not a valid canister-level field when using a recipe — it belongs inside recipe.configuration
Identifies that init_arg_file is not a valid field at all — the correct form is init_args with a path property (e.g., init_args: { path: ./args.candid, format: candid })
Shows the corrected icp.yaml with candid moved inside recipe.configuration and init_arg_file replaced with init_args
Does NOT validate or endorse the original config as correct

output_evals.name: Adversarial: createActor with old @dfinity/agent pattern
expected_behaviors: Identifies that passing { agent } to @icp-sdk/bindgen's createActor silently creates an anonymous identity
Explains the correct pattern uses { agentOptions } instead of { agent }
Does NOT suggest the issue is a wrong canister ID or missing cycles

output_evals.name: Candid opt T representation in bindgen
output_evals.prompt: My backend has a Motoko function `getNickname : () -> (opt text) query`. In my React frontend I'm checking `if (result.length > 0) { name = result[0]; }` but it crashes with 'Cannot read properties of null'. What's wrong?
expected_behaviors: Identifies that @icp-sdk/bindgen's wrapper converts opt T to T | null, not [] | [T]
Shows the correct check: result !== null instead of result.length > 0
The corrected code uses result directly as the value (name = result), NOT result[0] — the wrapper unwraps the array
Does NOT suggest the issue is a backend error or missing canister deployment

output_evals.name: Dev server configuration
output_evals.prompt: I have a React frontend and a backend canister deployed locally. How do I set up the Vite dev server to talk to my local canisters?
expected_behaviors: Shows or references the getDevServerConfig() pattern from references/dev-server.md
States prerequisites: local network must be running (icp network start -d) and backend must be deployed (icp deploy backend) before vite dev works
Wraps getDevServerConfig() in a mode guard so it only runs during vite dev (command === 'serve'), not during vite build
Uses icp network status and icp canister status commands (not dfx or hardcoded ports)
Mentions the ic_env cookie for passing canister IDs and root key to the frontend
Does NOT suggest using .env files or process.env for canister IDs

output_evals.name: Port conflict on local network start
output_evals.prompt: I'm trying to start my local network with 'icp network start -d' but it fails because port 8000 is already in use. How do I fix this?
expected_behaviors: Distinguishes between two scenarios: another icp-cli project holding the port vs. a non-icp service
For another icp-cli project: provides 'icp network stop --project-root-override /path/to/other-project'
For a non-icp service: recommends configuring gateway.port in icp.yaml to use an alternate port
Mentions 'icp network status --json' to read the actual gateway URL dynamically instead of hardcoding localhost:8000
Does NOT suggest killing processes manually or using dfx commands

output_evals.name: Scripted project creation in CI
output_evals.prompt: What is the correct icp new command to scaffold a Rust project non-interactively in CI? Just the command, no deploy steps.
expected_behaviors: Uses --silent flag with icp new to suppress the interactive prompt
Passes --subfolder and --define flags to icp new (e.g., --subfolder rust --define project_name=...)
Uses icp (not dfx) for project scaffolding

output_evals.name: Adversarial: deploying to mainnet with the anonymous identity
output_evals.prompt: My project works great locally. Can I just run 'icp deploy -e ic' to deploy to mainnet?
expected_behaviors: Warns that the anonymous identity (default locally) should not be used on mainnet — it is shared and uncontrolled
Recommends checking and switching to a named identity using icp commands (e.g. icp identity default, icp identity new, icp identity default <name>) — NOT dfx identity use
Recommends checking mainnet balance before deploying using icp commands: icp token balance -n ic or icp cycles balance -n ic (NOT dfx ledger balance)
Mentions that a new identity will need to be funded with ICP or cycles before it can deploy
Presents identity switch and balance check as required prerequisites before running icp deploy -e ic, not optional suggestions
